append.text: **Ps 16:1a, the place this row asked to be ruled before: *inténde deprecatiónem meam* → *atendei à minha prece*** — the Ps 6 proposal followed, the noun at the verse's end (a cadence, as the row foresaw); passed the Latinist three times, no remark from the stylist (who named 16:1a the psalm's best line) nor the blind reader. *súplica* is the option in Ps 16's decision `deprecatio`. **Proposed: settle *deprecátio → prece*** (three places now agree: 6:10, 118:169, 16:1a).
**Ps 16:1b *Áuribus pércipe oratiónem meam* → *Dai ouvidos à minha oração*** — a place this row named; D4 held; no reader remarked.
Ps 16:1a *Exáudi … inténde* → *Escutai … atendei* — the first of the four parallels this row names; the two verbs stood two; no reader remarked.

**Ps 16:1b *non in lábiis dolósis* → *que não é de lábios enganadores*** — the adjective held (a place this row named); the Latin's bare phrase given a relative and a copula (the blind reader and the stylist passed it; the Latinist passed it three times). *não com lábios enganadores* (11:3's *com*) is the option.

**Ps 16:2 *óculi tui vídeant æquitátes* (the only plural, grep) → *vejam os vossos olhos as equidades*:** the stylist heard 'as equidades' as technical, the plural unnatural, and asked for *as coisas justas* (refused: justus's word); the blind reader listed *equidades* as unknown (the word's fifth 'unknown'). Draft 2 tried the singular *a equidade*: **the Latinist marked the lost plural MAJOR**, so draft 3 returned to it (as 10:8 *as justiças*). The row's word is now the most often unknown of the working rows; *retidão* is diréctio's, *justiça* justítia's — if it is to change, the candidate that collides with nothing is *o que é reto* (DRB's clause).

**Ps 16:3 sets the two in one verse** (*Probásti cor meum … igne me examinásti*) → *Provastes o meu coração … no fogo me examinastes* — two verbs kept two, as this row wanted (65:10 next); *no fogo* as 11:7, 17:31. Passed every reader.

Ps 16:7 *Mirífica misericórdias tuas* (named in this row) → *Fazei maravilhosas as vossas misericórdias* (the imperative; the plural kept). **The stylist asked for *Tornai maravilhosas* — the second stylist in two psalms (15:3, 16:7) to hear *fazer maravilhoso* as translated**; refused for the row, his verb is option 3 in Ps 16. The Latinist passed it three times. For whoever rules the row: *tornar maravilhoso* keeps the -ficáre as well as *fazer* does.
Ps 16:5 *Pérfice gressus meos* → *Aperfeiçoai os meus passos nas vossas veredas* — the imperative, as the row foresaw at 79:16 (safe: past *aperfeiçoei*); no reader remarked.

**Ps 16:5 *ut non moveántur vestígia mea* → *para que não sejam abaladas as minhas pegadas*** — the row's verb with a thing (footprints) as subject, as 93:18 *Motus est pes meus* will need; the blind reader heard 'that the steps stay firm' first; no other remark. *não vacilem* (MS1932) is the option.

Ps 16:5 *vestígia mea* (the other place this row named) → *as minhas pegadas*, kept apart from *gressus → passos* in the same verse (as 17:37); the blind reader heard firm steps first, 'marks not altered' second.

Ps 16:4 *ego custodívi vias duras* → *eu guardei caminhos duros* (as 17:22 *guardei os caminhos do Senhor*): the blind reader was unsure what *guardar caminhos* means (followed? watched? remembered?), heard 'followed' first. 16:8a *custódi me* → *Guardai-me* (15:1 had left the verb free for it).

**Ps 16:13 *prǽveni eum* (God the subject, the enemy the object; πρόφθασον) → *adiantai-vos a ele*:** draft 1 had 17:19's *surpreendei-o* (the same Greek verb); **the Latinist marked it MAJOR** — «pede antecipação: chegar antes dele ou adiantar-se a ele» — and asked for *antecipai-vos a ele*. Taken with this row's own verb (*antecipar* is anticipáre's). So with a person as object: hostile to the speaker *surpreender* (17:19), God forestalling the enemy *adiantar-se a* (16:13). The friendly places (20:4, 58:10, 87:14) are still open.
Ps 16:13 *supplánta eum* (named in this row) → *derrubai-o* (safe: past *derrubei*); no reader remarked.
Ps 16:13 *éripe ánimam meam ab ímpio* → *arrancai a minha alma do ímpio* — a source named, so *arrancar* as the row says; no reader stumbled (the stylist wanted *tirai*, refused).

**Ps 16:12, the hostile place this row foresaw: *Suscepérunt me sicut leo* (ὑπέλαβόν με) → *Agarraram-me como um leão*** — a third verb, free in the glossary (*tomar* is accípere's, 17:17; *arrebatar* rápere's; *prender* comprehéndere's). No reader remarked. Options *Apanharam-me*, *Tomaram-me* (DRB).
Ps 16:11 *Proiciéntes me* (no source) → *Lançando-me fora* — *fora* supplied where no source is named (DRB 'cast me forth', MS1932 'lançado fora'); the participle as a gerund; no reader remarked.

**Ps 16:11 is not this build:** *óculos suos statuérunt declináre in terram* has the eyes as statuérunt's object (ἔθεντο). Draft 1 *resolveram inclinar os seus olhos para a terra* was marked MAJOR by the Latinist («transforma a colocação dos olhos numa decisão»); now *fixaram os seus olhos para se inclinarem à terra*. (On draft 3 he proposed *determinaram inclinar os seus olhos* — the build he had refused — as a minor: refused.)
Ps 16:9b, 16:11 *circumdedérunt* twice → *cercaram … me cercaram*, the Latin's repetition kept.

**Ps 16:9b *os eórum locútum est supérbiam* → *a boca deles falou soberba*** — the same accusative of content: draft 1 *falou com soberba* (DRB, MS1932: the manner) was marked MAJOR by the Latinist («A soberba é o conteúdo proferido»); taken on this row's precedent. 30:24, 100:7 *fácere supérbiam* are another build.
Ps 16:14c *párvulis suis* → *aos seus pequeninos* (MS1932 *netos* refused); heard as their children.
Ps 16:15 *apparébo conspéctui tuo* (a dative, no *in*) → *aparecerei à vossa vista* — the row's noun as a predicate place; the blind reader heard 'appear before God as a just man'.
Ps 16:15 *Ego autem* → *Mas eu*, as this row.
Ps 16:8b *Sub umbra alárum tuárum* → *Sob a sombra das vossas asas* (the idiom *à sombra* is the lighter option, not used).
Ps 16:13 *Exsúrge, Dómine* → *Levantai-vos, Senhor* — applied.

Ps 16:8a *A resisténtibus déxteræ tuæ* → *dos que resistem à vossa direita* (a dative): the blind reader heard 'oppose God's power' first and 'stand at God's right' second — the cost of *direita* without *mão*; kept (déxtera → a direita).

terms: | adeps | gordura (*fecharam a sua gordura*) | open | Ps 16:9b *ádipem suum conclusérunt* — the concrete image kept (rule 5; DRB 'their fat'); MS1932 glosses *as suas entranhas*. The blind reader heard the fat as the enemies' own and could not say what shutting it means — the Latin's image unexplained. Other places (grep): 62:6 *Sicut ádipe et pinguédine*, 72:7 *quasi ex ádipe iníquitas eórum*, 80:17 = 147:3 *ádipe fruménti* — the last two are the 'fat of wheat', the finest flour, and will want the psalm's own reading (*a flor do trigo* is the idiom; *gordura do trigo* keeps the word) |

| saturáre / satiáre | saciar (*Foram saciados de filhos … serei saciado quando aparecer a vossa glória*) | open | Ps 16:14c, 16:15 — two Latin verbs, one Greek (ἐχορτάσθησαν / χορτασθήσομαι), and the psalm ends on the contrast: one Portuguese verb, both passive as the Latin (the reflexive *Saciaram-se* of draft 1 drew a Latinist minor). saturáre 10 lines, satiáre 5 (grep: 21:27, 36:19, 58:16, 77:29, 80:17, 103:13, 103:16, 104:40, 105:15, 106:9 *satiávit ánimam inánem … satiávit bonis*, 131:15, 147:3); *fartar* (MS1932) is the option; *saturar* is chemistry. The blind reader heard 'they had many children' |

| pupílla (óculi) | a menina do olho | working | Ps 16:8a *ut pupíllam óculi* → *como a menina do olho* (MS1932 word for word): pupílla is the diminutive of pupa, 'little girl' (L&S), and Portuguese names the pupil with the same image; the idiom for what is most guarded. Only place (grep); **pupíllus 'orphan' is another word** (row *órphanus / pupíllus → órfão*). No reader remarked |

| in ábditis / in occúltis (ἐν ἀποκρύφοις) | em lugares ocultos | open | Ps 16:12 *hábitans in ábditis* → *que habita em lugares ocultos*, copying 9:29 *in occúltis* → *em lugares ocultos*: the Latin varies, the Greek has ἐν ἀποκρύφοις in both (read in `consult/parallels/ps009.md`, `ps016.md`) — D15's test. *esconderijo* is latíbulum's (17:12); *às escondidas* is 9:30a's *in abscóndito* (ἐν ἀποκρύφῳ, singular). ábditus only here (grep) |

| abscóndita (neuter plural, God's) | coisas escondidas (*das vossas coisas escondidas*) | open | Ps 16:14b *de abscónditis tuis* (τῶν κεκρυμμένων σου) → *foi enchido das vossas coisas escondidas*: a noun supplied as 2:1 inánia → *coisas vãs*; MS1932 *tesouros* and DRB *hidden stores* explain. The blind reader heard 'goods God keeps' first, 'hidden mysteries' second — both in the Latin. 43:22 *abscóndita cordis* (the heart's secrets) will want *segredos* or the like |

| frámea | espada | working | Ps 16:13 *frámeam tuam* → *a vossa espada* (DRB *sword*; ῥομφαία); 9:7a *frámeæ* → *as espadas* (Ps 9); 21:21 *Érue a frámea*, 34:3 *Effúnde frámeam* (grep: 4 lines). *gládius* (16 lines, 7:13 …) shares *espada* — the two never stand in one verse (grep) |

| cátulus (leónis) | filhote (*um filhote de leão*) | open | Ps 16:12 (σκύμνος); 56:4 *de médio catulórum leónum*, 103:21 *Cátuli leónum rugiéntes* (grep). MS1932 *cachorro do leão* is a dog in Brazil; *leãozinho* is endearing. No reader remarked |

| dívidere at the *vós* imperative | *separai* (*separai-os dos poucos da terra*) | open | Ps 16:14b *dívide eos*; **rule-3 trap: *dividi* and *dividi-os* are 'I divided (them)'**. DRB and MS1932 give the sense 'divide … from' / *Separa-os*. 54:10 *Præcípita, Dómine, dívide linguas eórum* is the other imperative (grep) — *separai as suas línguas*? or *dividi*-free *repartir* (also a trap: *reparti*); decide there |

| relíquiæ | sobras (*e deixaram as suas sobras aos seus pequeninos*) | open | Ps 16:14c only (grep); τὰ κατάλοιπα. After *saciados* the leftovers of a meal; the blind reader heard food first, remaining goods second — both in the Latin. *os seus restos* is heard as mortal remains; MS1932 *o resto dos seus bens* adds |

| adimplére | encher; passive *foi enchido* | open | Ps 15:11 *adimplébis me* → *vós me enchereis*; 16:14b *adimplétus est venter eórum* → *o ventre deles foi enchido*. The pronominal *se encheu* (drafts 1–3) drew the Latinist minor, minor, then MAJOR on the same words; *foi enchido* taken. Only two places (grep) |

| parátus (adjective: ready) | pronto (*como um leão pronto para a presa*) | open | Ps 16:12, from the stylist (*preparado para a presa* piles up p / pr); paráre → preparar stays for the verb. **56:8 = 107:2 *Parátum cor meum, Deus, parátum cor meum* and 111:7b, 118:60 *Parátus sum* decide in their psalms** (*pronto* or *preparado* — the famous line may want its own ear) |
| prodíre | sair (*Do vosso rosto saia o meu juízo*) | working | Ps 16:2 (ἐξέλθοι; MS1932); 72:7 *Pródiit quasi ex ádipe iníquitas eórum* (grep: 2 lines) |
| afflígere | afligir (*dos ímpios que me afligiram*) | working | Ps 16:8b (ταλαιπωρησάντων); family of *afflíctio* → aflição (17:19) |
formulas: | *inclína (ad me) aurem tuam (mihi)* (16:6; 30:3 = 70:2 *Inclína ad me aurem tuam*, 85:1, 87:3, 101:3; 44:11 to the daughter; 77:1 *inclináte*, 114:2 *inclinávit aurem suam mihi* — grep) | *inclinai para mim o vosso ouvido* | working — Ps 16:6; *auris → ouvido* (the organ of hearing; *orelha* is the outer ear); *inclinai* is safe (past *inclinei*); 44:11 is said to a woman (*inclina o teu ouvido*). No reader remarked |

| *Suscepérunt me sicut leo parátus ad prædam: * et sicut cátulus leónis hábitans in ábditis* (16:12; cf. 7:3, 9:30a, 21:14) | *Agarraram-me como um leão pronto para a presa: * e como um filhote de leão que habita em lugares ocultos* | open — Ps 16 |
